notes: Single source of truth for the Sienna unit vocabulary. 'dimension' is an exponent map over base dimensions M (mass, kg), L (length, m), T (time, s), I (electric current, A), and pseudo-dimensions USD (money) and Btu (fuel chemical energy, kept distinct from electrical energy so heat-rate and fuel-intensity quantities never collide with cost quantities). Dimensionless quantities use the empty exponent map {} and the single allowed unit "1"; percent is banned (store fractions). 'to_default' in allowed_units is the exact multiplicative factor converting a value in 'unit' to the quantity's default_unit; it is null where conversion is context-dependent rather than a fixed factor (e.g. pu bases), and 0.0 where this layer deliberately does not perform the conversion at all. Angle carries real factors (rad is the default, deg is pi/180) so that source data in degrees converts on the way in rather than being rejected. For Frequency/Hz, to_default instead records the nominal system frequency (60.0), not a conversion factor. Time is deliberately split across three quantity types, each with exactly one allowed unit so the vocabulary itself enforces the tier: Duration (seconds) for continuous-time constants, OperationalDuration (minutes) for scheduling and commitment durations, and CalendarPeriod (years) for long-term planning spans. The tier fixes the unit, not the numeric type: only CalendarPeriod is integer throughout, while OperationalDuration is real except where a field is genuinely discrete. Hours are not a vocabulary unit -- an hours-valued field is a tier error, not a conversion. Only min -> s is an exact physical factor; years are not bridged at all. 'ucum' carries the UCUM code of the default_unit where one exists, else null.

quantity_types.name: ActivePowerChangeRate
quantity_types.description: Rate of change of active power (ramp)

quantity_types.name: FractionPerTime
quantity_types.description: A fraction of a stored quantity lost or decayed per unit of time (storage self-discharge, leakage). Per minute, matching OperationalDuration: the value multiplies the simulation step, so its time basis must be the same one durations use or the decay is wrong by the ratio of the two. Distinct from Frequency despite sharing the T^-1 dimension.

quantity_types.name: PowerPerFrequency
quantity_types.description: Active power response per unit of frequency deviation (regulation / droop participation)

quantity_types.name: Duration
quantity_types.description: Continuous-time duration or time constant, real-valued seconds. Dynamics time constants are inherently fractional, so no integer representation exists for them. Discrete scheduling durations use OperationalDuration; multi-year planning spans use CalendarPeriod.

quantity_types.name: OperationalDuration
quantity_types.description: Operational or scheduling duration, expressed in minutes. The unit is the convention; integrality is not. Most of these fields are real-valued because the data model library validates them on an open (0, nothing) range and sub-minute products are legitimate (a 30-second reserve, a fractional-minute saturation window). Declare a field integer only where the domain is genuinely discrete and the ingest path rounds -- no current field qualifies. Sub-minute control timing belongs in Duration instead.

quantity_types.name: CalendarPeriod
quantity_types.description: Long-term planning span, a whole number of years. Integer-valued. Deliberately carries no to_default bridge into Duration or OperationalDuration: a calendar year is not a fixed number of seconds, so any such factor would silently bake in a 365-day convention. 'ucum' is null for the same reason: every UCUM year atom is longer than 365 days (a/a_j = 365.25, a_g = 365.2425, a_t = 365.24219), so none of them matches the 365-day year this vocabulary actually uses. Emitting "a" would hand a consumer a leap-day convention we do not follow.

quantity_types.name: Fraction
quantity_types.description: Fractional quantity (efficiency, losses, cofire level, etc.)

quantity_types.name: HeatRate
quantity_types.description: Heat rate (fuel energy per unit of electrical energy)

quantity_types.name: StartFuelPerCapacity
quantity_types.description: Start-up fuel per unit of capacity

quantity_types.name: HeadRate
quantity_types.description: Rate of change of hydraulic head

quantity_types.name: CostPerCapacity
quantity_types.description: Cost per unit of capacity (capital cost)

quantity_types.name: CostPerEnergy
quantity_types.description: Cost per unit of energy (operation / energy capital cost)

quantity_types.name: CO2Emissions
quantity_types.description: CO2 emission rate (mass per unit of fuel energy)

quantity_types.name: CostPerVolume
quantity_types.description: Cost per unit of volume (e.g. reservoir operation cost)

quantity_types.name: CostPerLevel
quantity_types.description: Cost per unit of hydraulic head (e.g. reservoir operation cost when level_data_type=HEAD)

quantity_types.name: EmissionRate
quantity_types.description: Emission mass per unit of electrical energy

quantity_types.name: CostPerMass
quantity_types.description: Cost per unit of mass (e.g. carbon price or tax)
